hide.eDamageStone.ilmColumnsShareOneFlag.formula: =IFS(OR($EH5, FB$2), , EPG_UW_TARGET_LEVEL(CH5+1, "Inner Land Mines", "Quantity", $AY$23), , DVT_UW_STAT("Inner Land Mines", "Quantity", CH5+1)="", , TRUE, LET(...))

traps.note: FB5, FC5, FD5 and FE5 ALL open with OR($EH5, FB$2) - the ILM Damage flag. Every other column in the band reads its own. Inert today because FB2:FE2 are the identical expression =AND(NOT($BH$37)), which is exactly why it is invisible: a change to FC2, FD2 or FE2 would have no effect. Recorded as read, not filed as a defect to fix on a sheet that is not ours.

The level is parsed out of a STRING by taking its first two characters: VALUE(LEFT(IDS_UW_LEVEL(...), 2)). A level of 100 or more would read as its first two digits. Whether that is reachable depends on the maximum UW stat level, which is NOT established here - the sim columns stop when DVT_UW_STAT(..., level+1) returns empty, so the bound lives in DVT_UWs. Flagged as a hazard with the check named, not as a live defect.
Every UW stat reads 0 on the demo IDS attached to this copy. A truncation or an off-by-one in this parse cannot show up at level 0, so this column cannot be validated against the sheet as it stands.

FIVE columns wrap the parse in IFERROR(..., -1): SM Cover Fire (BX), SL Light Range (CB), PS Death Creep (CF), ILM Charged Mines (CJ) and CF Chrono Loop (CL). -1 means NOT UNLOCKED, and it is not 0 - the consumers test IF(BX5>-1, ...), IF(CB5=-1, 1, ...) and IF(CJ5=-1, 1, ...). A port that defaults a locked UW+ stat to 0 makes it look owned at level zero, which is a different thing from absent.

The one path item with a ROI column and NO simulation column. There are 29 level columns (BO:CQ) and 29 ROI columns (FM:GO) but only 28 simulations (EJ:FK); GK computes its ROI in one step instead of simulating a row.

It also divides by CS5, the current module bonus, where every other ROI column divides by $EE5, the current eDMG. Equivalent for a pure multiplier, but it means GK is not comparable to the others by inspection - the denominators differ.

gate.eDamageStone.moduleLevelCaps.label: Assist module hard level caps
gate.eDamageStone.moduleLevelCaps.formula: =IFS(OR($EH5, FH$2), , CN5>=69, , TRUE, LET(SubstatAssistCap, EPG_ASSIST_SUB_CAP($AN$23, CN5+1, $BC$45), ...))

traps.note: The four module columns cap at a HARD LEVEL - CN 69, CO 69, CP 99, CQ 69 - and never call EPG_UW_TARGET_LEVEL. So Ignore UW Target Levels does not reach them: it is a UW-stat switch, not a path-wide one. Stone cost for a module level is 12 + 3*(level+1).
The 25th of the 29 level columns, and the only one with no simulation column. Its ROI is computed directly at GK5.
Five module levels read straight off the mirrored BL column, not parsed from a string the way the 24 UW stat levels are. Different source, different failure mode.

NOT a level, despite sitting in the level band BQ5:CD5 under the header "UW CD". It is MAX of three cooldowns in SECONDS, each 300-10*level (200 for Black Hole). Reading the band as levels because thirteen of its fourteen entries are levels gets this one wrong by two orders of magnitude.

stat.eEconStones.uwCooldownBundle.label: UW CD bundle upgrade
stat.eEconStones.uwCooldownBundle.formula: =IFS(OR(DW$2, $DL5), , CA5<110, , TRUE, LET(Old, DD5, GTcdNext, IF(CA5>DVT_UW_STAT("Golden Tower", "Cooldown", BS5), 0, 1), BHcdNext, IF(CA5>DVT_UW_STAT("Black Hole", "Cooldown", BV5), 0, 1), DWcdNext, IF(CA5>DVT_UW_STAT("Death Wave", "Cooldown", BX5), 0, 1), ..., GTCost, IF(AND(HasGT, GTcdNext), DVT_UW_COST("Golden Tower", "Cooldown", BS5+1), 0), BHCost, IF(AND(HasBH, BHcdNext), DVT_UW_COST("Black Hole", "Cooldown", BV5+1), 0), DWCost, IF(AND(HasDW, DWcdNext), DVT_UW_COST("Death Wave", "Cooldown", BX5+1), 0), (New/Old-1)/(GTCost+BHCost+DWCost)))

traps.note: A BUNDLE: one path row that buys the GT, BH and DW cooldown upgrades TOGETHER. Its cost is the SUM of the three next-level costs, and each is counted only when its next level actually improves the synced cooldown (GTcdNext / BHcdNext / DWcdNext). Modelling the three cooldowns as independent path items both double-counts them and loses this row.
Offered only when Keep GT|BH|DW CD Synced is on (DW2 = OR(NOT(AZ17), CA5<110)) AND the synced cooldown is at least 110s. Below 110 the row is blank.

display.eEconStones.uwLevelColumns.label: UW level columns (BQ5:CD5), at GT Cooldown

LEFT(EA4, LEN(EA4)-8) strips the literal " Mastery" - eight characters - off the column header to recover the card name. A renamed header breaks the lookup silently.

The five mastery columns have NO level column: the band BQ5:CD5 is fourteen wide and the path is nineteen. Their ROI reads a precomputed cell on the eEcon panel ($AX$32, $AX$34, ...), so the work happens on eEcon and only the column appears here.

stat.eEconDiscount.multiplierRoi.label: Workshop Utility discount ROI
stat.eEconDiscount.multiplierRoi.formula: =IFS(OR(CL$2, $CJ5), , EPG_LEVEL_CHECK(BP5+1, $BE$11, $BF$11), , TRUE, LET(Old, BW5, New, 1/(1-(BP5+1)*0.5%), Dur, LABDURATION_SINGLE_ADJUSTED($CL$4, BP5+1), (New/Old-1)/Dur))

traps.note: (New/Old-1) - the RISING form. This column is a MULTIPLIER, 1/(1-lvl*0.5%). The five columns beside it are COSTS and use (Old/New-1), the falling form. One ratio direction for the whole band is wrong for five of six columns, and both forms return a positive number, so nothing looks broken.

stat.eEconDiscount.costRoi.label: Labs Coin Discount ROI

traps.note: (Old/New-1) - the FALLING form, because EPC_LAB_DISCOUNT returns a COST that goes down. Paired with CL5 deliberately: the two are adjacent, look identical in shape, and differ in the one place that matters.
Also carries a category guard the multiplier column does not: CK5<>"Laboratory" blanks it. The discount columns are not interchangeable rows of one table.

The level is INFERRED BY DIVISION: the vault stat over its per-level step. Nothing stores it. The step differs per stat - 5%, 1%, 5%, 2%, 5%, 5%, 4%, 5%, 4%, 4%, 5% - so a single divisor is wrong for eight of eleven columns.
A stat that is not an exact multiple of its step yields a FRACTIONAL level, and the consumers use it as an exponent (POW(2, BO5)) and an index. Nothing rounds it.
The ONE discount column whose hide flag does NOT carry AY14 (eEcon AZ14, Hide Retroactive Discount Labs). Five of the six do. "Hide retroactive discount labs" is not "hide the discount block".

display.eDamage.coinPathHeader.label: Coin path header, with no path under it

The block under this header is empty in BOTH formula and value mode - checked both ways, because formula mode alone cannot tell an empty cell from a mirrored one.

eHP mirrors both its satellites back and eEcon mirrors both of its own. eDamage is the only planner tab that computes a path on a satellite and does not display it. eDamage Coins is a HIDDEN tab, so that path is reachable by no ordinary route, while eDamage!AY27 still offers a control that only eDamage Coins reads.

lambda.workbook.moduleLevelLimit.label: EPG_MODULE_LEVEL_LIMIT
lambda.workbook.moduleLevelLimit.formula: LAMBDA(input_text, LET(raw, IFERROR(INDEX(SPLIT(input_text, " "), 1), input_text), IFS(raw="none", 0, raw="all", 300, ISNUMBER(raw), raw, TRUE, 0)))

traps.note: Turns a DROPDOWN LABEL into a NUMBER: it splits on space, takes the first token, and maps "none" to 0, "all" to 300, a numeric token to itself, and anything else to 0. So "All         | Show all labs levels on Coin path" is 300 and "None | ..." is 0.

The consumers use it as a HORIZON, not a visibility flag: BP$5 + EPG_MODULE_LEVEL_LIMIT($AY$27) <= BP5 blanks the column. It caps how many levels PAST the current one the path will plan. A boolean model of these controls loses every value between 0 and 300.
The fallback for an unrecognised label is 0, which is the same as "none" - a renamed or reordered dropdown option silently plans nothing rather than erroring.

display.eDamage.moduleLevelHorizon.label: Module level horizon (eDamage)
display.eDamage.moduleLevelHorizon.formula: =IF('Master Sheet'!I7>159, "All         | Show all levels on path", "")

traps.note: A FORMULA, not a dropdown a player sets. It yields the "All" label once Master Sheet I7 - the CANNON module level - passes 159, and an EMPTY STRING otherwise. eHP!AM4 is the identical shape keyed on I23, the ARMOR module level. eEcon!AZ12 is the only one of the three that is a literal, and so the only user-settable module horizon on the workbook.

EPG_MODULE_LEVEL_LIMIT("") is 0, so below level 160 the module path plans NOTHING. eHP Coins gates the same thing a second way with BU5<160, which is how the two agree without referring to each other.

The ONE column of twenty-five that divides by $CT5. Every other ROI on the tab divides by $EC5, the current eDMG. Cash Bonus is measured against a different baseline, and nothing in the column shape says so - it is one cell reference apart from its neighbours.

A FORMULA, not a switch: =NOT(EQ(AX20, "Tourney")). Perks are on for every run type EXCEPT Tourney, and AX20 is itself derived from Run Type. Typed as a control here until a capture script wrote to it and read back a formula. The eEcon and eHP perks masters are literals; eDamage is the odd one.

hide.eDamage.improveTradeOffPerksColumn.label: Improve Trade-off Perks column hidden
hide.eDamage.improveTradeOffPerksColumn.formula: =OR(NOT(AND($AY$61, $AY$65)), $AX$19="Attack Disso", EPG_LEVEL_CHECK(BC29+1, BD29, BE29), AND($AY$26, NOT(IDS_LAB_HAS_UNLOCKED(FY4))))

traps.note: Read back from the sheet on 2026-08-19 to check the port’s prerequisite, after the neighbouring Demon Mode Mastery gate (GA2) turned out to cite a formula nobody had verified. This one AND-s the perks master with the row, exactly as the port has it — so it is NOT the cause of the Improve Trade-off Perks mismatches in the parity sweep.

stat.eDamage.critChanceMasteryShadow.label: Critical Chance Mastery shadow column
stat.eDamage.critChanceMasteryShadow.formula: =IFS(OR($EU5, EV$2), , EPG_LEVEL_CHECK(BU5+1, $BD$40, $BE$40), , TRUE, LET(SubstatAssistCap, EPG_ASSIST_SUB_CAP($AN$4, $BL$42, CO5), Substat, $AM$15 + SubstatAssistCap * $AO$15, CardCCMastery, 1+(1%*(1+BU5+1)), CC, DJ5+1%, CF, DK5, SCC, DL5+1%, SCM, ($AN$68*(1+(2%*BX5))+Substat)*$BK$21*(1+$BL$21)*(1+$BM$21)*CardCCMastery, UWCrit, EPD_UWCRITICAL(CC, CF, SCC, SCM), BulletCrit, EPD_CRITICAL(CC, CF, SCC, SCM, IF($AM$7+$AR$7, 5, 0)), DI5 * (BulletCrit * EA5 * ED5 + EO5 * UWCrit)*ER$5))

traps.note: A SHADOW column: it rebuilds the whole of ES5 with one Critical Chance Mastery level bumped, and that is how the sheet prices the candidate. It does not call EPD_CRIT_CHANCE — it writes CC, DJ5+1% flat.

That disagrees with the base column. EPD_CRIT_CHANCE nests the mastery inside IF(has_card, ...) with has_card = AND($AY$39, $AY$47), so with the cards master OFF the base credits nothing while this shadow credits a percentage point per level. The sheet therefore buys the mastery on an estimate its own next row will not deliver. Measured on a swept account: shadow 1.83674216e-2 against a base recompute of 1.28635275e-2, a ratio of 1.4278.

Passes the player's FIXED core bonuses $AM$23 / $AO$23. The coin tab's counterpart (stat.eDamageCoins.coreModulePair) re-derives both from module rarity at the levels its own path buys, so the two tabs' Core factors genuinely differ. Read live 2026-08-20: eDamage $AM$23 = 1.505 against the coin tab's 1.04.

stat.eDamageCoins.coreModulePair.label: Core module pair (eDamage Coins, derived from rarity at level)

traps.note: RE-DERIVES the core bonuses from module rarity at CE5/CF5, the levels the coin path can buy, where eDamage passes the fixed $AM$23. Live 2026-08-20: MODSTAT_CORE(IDS_MOD_CORE_RARITY(IDS_MOD_CORE_NAME($AX$15)), CE5) = 1.04 against eDamage's 1.505, and 1.505/1.04 = 1.44712 -- exactly the ratio the port carried against the sheet's UWs on all 33 swept accounts, because the Core factor multiplies the whole UWAdditionalDMG term.

On the oracle working copy IDS_MOD_CORE_NAME($AX$15) resolves to "Any Other" and hence rarity "Common", because nothing is imported behind IDS -- the same degradation already documented for IDS_LAB_LEVEL. The assist name resolves to null.

First column of the coin level band BO5:CM5, which is an exact 1:1 in column order with EffectiveDamageCoinLevels. Row 6 is BO5+FZ5, so the band is the path's running level. (2) Those, and its CardCCMastery, are applied UNCONDITIONALLY where the base column gates the mastery on the card being equipped. (3) Its SCM substat is `$AM$15 + $AR$15`, and $AR$15 is the UNIQUE assist column rather than the substat one -- row 15 carries no unique, so $AR$15 is 0 and the assist half of the substat vanishes. Live 2026-08-20: $AM$15 = 0.3769, $AO$15 = 0.09, cap = 0.23, so the candidate uses 0.3769 against the base row's 0.3976. That $AR$15 is the reference candidate-vs-base-diff.mjs flags on this column.

The three cannot be reproduced piecemeal, and the measurements say so. Nothing reproduced: 1.031x..1.411x of the sheet's ROI across 32 accounts. Adding the two flat one-percents alone: up to 1.502x, WORSE. Adding the dropped assist substat alone: 0.509x..0.687x, overshooting. A five percent change in one term swings the ROI by fifty because the gain is a small difference of two large numbers, so the column is all-or-nothing. Left unreproduced deliberately -- it is never the best candidate on any of the 33 swept accounts, and tuning toward a middle value would be fitting a constant rather than reading the sheet.
